newsitem.title: UK: Mark near high on crosses, cheered by dollar drop.
newsitem.headline: Mark near high on crosses, cheered by dollar drop.

text.p: The mark was near its session peaks against most European currencies in late trade, helped by declines of the dollar and sterling from multi-year highs against the mark.
Traders said that with the market's attention firmly fixed on the dollar and sterling, moves in the European crosses were quite mild today.

"It's been fairly quiet on the mark crosses as people are following the dollar/mark. The mark was quite well bid (on the crosses) when it was well bid on the dollar, but otherwise it's been uneventful," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London.
The mark was at 3.3765/70 French francs at 1540 GMT, up a touch from 3.3757/62 in Tuesday's late trade, while mark/Swiss was at its session high of 85.92/95 against 85.79/82 on Tuesday.
Traders said the mark's bearish tone on the crosses changed when the Bundesbank issued a statement saying it was not of the opinion that the dollar should rise further.
The comment knocked the dollar off its 34-month high of 1.6935 marks and sterling/mark off its 52-month peak of 2.7685.

Comments from Italian and French ministers that their countries were determined to meet EMU budget deficit criteria to join the single European currency in the first round did not have much impact on the mark crosses.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said Italy would meet the three-percent budget deficit-to-GDP ratio in time to join EMU in 1999.

French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said France's deficit ratio was 4.1 percent in 1996, just over the government's target of 4.0. He also said he was prepared to freeze spending in this year's budget to meet the EMU criteria.
Mark/lira was at 981.20/50, up from late Tuesday's 979.50/98.
